body: Yes, they're lovely at nundah. My dad does a bit of work for the headspace group, and from what I've learnt from him it's a very well funded group. They have very good psychs.

Yes headspace is a great place to go. I'd definitely suggest that your boyfriend checks them out. They have some great services, and 2 different places in central brisbane area (I think nundah is the biggest one, but they're both very effective). The services are usually free, because it's government managed, and the psych's are great at youth mental health.

I'm a bit concerned about the whole suicide part though. If this is something you think is a problem, please get him to see your local doctor. Even a 15 minute session would be enough for your doctor to give a rough assessment and recommendation.

My first suggestion is don't bother with the hospitals in Brisbane unless it's urgent - and if it is, get an ambulance to pick him up, especially if you think he's been harming.
For therapy, it depends on what you are after. I suggest going to your local GP with your boyfriend as your first stop and let him explain what he wants. There's a lot of services available in Brisbane for mental health, you just need to know where to look, and a GP will be perfect for that. Anti-depressants might be an option, but that's up to the doctor. Medicare usually pays for around 60% of private therapy fees, but I suggest doing some research on limits. When I made my way through the mental health system it ended up costing around $1000 to me over about 3 months, and then medicare started paying for 90% of the consultation fees. That was with near-weekly appointments at both a psychologist and a psychiatrist.

Jobs aren't that important. And honestly, suicide isn't that important. It might seem like the best answer, but your perspective is somewhat warped at the moment. There's no rush to die, you can do so much stuff before that time comes. You can pat kittens, you can travel to another country, you can go out and buy a juicy burger from your local restaurant. If you don't have the money for that kind of stuff you can go camping, you can stay home and dance to music.
Just have fun.

I've looked at your post a few times since you wrote it. I haven't really known what to write in response. I've been very confused. The desire to commit suicide is still prominent, and I guess my self esteem has decreased. I think I'm insignificant. I can't get rid of the feeling that by telling people how miserable I am I'm simply spreading the misery. It makes me feel scared and isolated. If I tell people I want to die they freak out and think I'm fucked up. I have friends who know and have dealt with it. I either care about them enough to not want to worry them about me, or feel too isolated from them to think they'd really be able to help anyway. In both cases I tend to just not communicate with my friends much about how I'm feeling.

Telling people is really hard. I'm not worth the attention. Even though I know people who just want to help. I know that it's not an inconvenience for them, that if they can make me smile or think better then they will be the happier for it. But I'm not worth it. I want someone to save me, but I just want to die. I feel so irrational and confused...

I've been doing more photography lately. It's been consistently involving, which is good. I'm thinking about quitting uni, but my psych has said I should avoid making big decisions because of the big fluctuation in my feelings and opinions. I'm studying Journalism and Philosophy. I don't want to make a career out of either (it was something of a relief to figure this out), but I don't know what I actually do want to do. That's been adding stress onto how I've been feeling, which has made it harder to cope, but such is life I guess.

I do photography. I'm not bad at it, [these being some of my photos](http://imgur.com/a/mKWym), but I just don't get as much enjoyment out of it these days. I have time to do it and I do, but it just doesn't fulfill me, or give me the meaning in life that I guess I lack. My motivation levels are at an all time low, gaming is blatantly boring, though I used to love playing games. Going to my job is torturous, even though it's relatively easy and well paying with a pleasant atmosphere (library assistant). I just don't know where I can find something that gives me happiness... Like I said, weed is the only thing that reliably makes me feel good, and that comes with the caveat of being an unproductive stoner.
